headline: Walmart adds Apple Pay and Google Pay support by end of 2026
summary: After years of resistance, the retail giant is finally rolling out tap-to-pay options to all US stores, aiming for full integration by the end of 2026.
details: Walmart announced it will begin offering tap-to-pay options, including Apple Pay and Google Pay, at select locations starting August 24th. This move marks a significant shift for the retail giant, which has historically resisted supporting these popular mobile payment methods.

The company plans to expand tap-to-pay support to all its US stores by the end of 2026, with gas stations to follow by mid-2027. This rollout aims to provide customers with more payment choices, aligning with Walmart's stated goal of allowing shoppers to "check out in the way that works best for them."

This decision comes after years of Walmart championing its own payment system, Walmart Pay, launched in 2016, and even backing the now-defunct CurrentC mobile payment service. A Walmart spokesperson had previously stated that existing options like Walmart Pay were sufficient, but the company has now changed its strategy.

The integration of Apple Pay and Google Pay is expected to enhance the checkout experience for millions of Walmart shoppers, offering a more convenient and modern payment solution alongside traditional methods like cash and credit cards.
